long_biography.plain_text:
Sergey Adonyev backed Skartel, the operator behind Yota, as Russia moved towards fourth-generation mobile broadband. The company launched WiMAX service in 2008, then replaced its Moscow network with LTE. This combination of network investment and a simplified consumer offer made Yota his defining technology venture.

Adonyev had previously co-founded Olbi-Jazz, an importer of fruit and sugar, before shifting into telecommunications through Telconet Capital. Inside Yota, the subscriber-device division became the separate Yota Devices business and developed the dual-screen YotaPhone. Adonyev and his partners sold their operator holding in 2013, while the hardware company continued under a different shareholder structure.
long_biography.html:
Sergey Adonyev backed Skartel, the operator behind Yota, as Russia moved towards fourth-generation mobile broadband. The company launched WiMAX service in 2008, then replaced its Moscow network with LTE. This combination of network investment and a simplified consumer offer made Yota his defining technology venture.

Adonyev had previously co-founded Olbi-Jazz, an importer of fruit and sugar, before shifting into telecommunications through Telconet Capital. Inside Yota, the subscriber-device division became the separate Yota Devices business and developed the dual-screen YotaPhone. Adonyev and his partners sold their operator holding in 2013, while the hardware company continued under a different shareholder structure.
